questions.prompt: What is the difference between a parameter and an argument?
options: Parameter is in the definition, argument is the value passed
Argument is in the definition, parameter is the value
Parameters are for classes, arguments are for structs
questions.explanation: A parameter is the variable in the method signature; an argument is the actual value passed at the call site.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: void Connect(_____ server, int port) { ... }
Arrange the pieces of a method definition with two parameters.
What does the params keyword allow?
options: Passing a variable number of arguments
questions.explanation: params allows a method to accept a variable number of arguments of the same type as an array.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: void Log(_____ message) { Console.WriteLine(message); }
Write a method SetName with an optional second parameter title that defaults to "Mr.". Print the full name.
Can named arguments change the order of arguments when calling a method?
options: Yes, named arguments can appear in any order
questions.explanation: Named arguments allow you to pass values in any order because each value is explicitly matched to a parameter name.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Calculate(_____: 10, y: 20);
Arrange the call styles for a method with parameters x and y.
Can you pass fewer arguments than required by a params array?
options: No, you must pass at least one
questions.explanation: A params parameter can receive zero arguments. If you pass zero, the method receives an empty array.
